newsitem.title: USA: Most time spent waiting to see doctors -- U.S. poll.
newsitem.headline: Most time spent waiting to see doctors -- U.S. poll.

text.p: Many U.S. medical patients spend twice as much time waiting to see their physicians as they with them a national poll released Monday.

Of 1,014 adults surveyed, 49 percent said they spend 20 minutes or more in their doctors' waiting room, while 54 percent said they wait at least another 10 minutes in the examining room before the physician arrives.
The majority of those surveyed said they spend less than 15 minutes actually with their physicians.

"Today's poll illustrates the need to make improvements in health care efficiency, like reducing waiting time," said Rod Nelson, president of ATAC CPA Health Network, a group of accountants that sponsored the survey.

What time patients actually have with their physicians was seen as worthwhile, the study found. Forty-nine percent of those surveyed rated their physician "excellent" or "good" at listening to and answering questions.

Nelson made his remarks here at the 1997 Conference for CPA/Medical Practice Consultants. The poll was conducted by telephone July 11 to 13 among adults aged 18 and older. The margin of error was three percentage points with a 95 percent confidence level, said ATAC CPA Health Network, formed by accountants who work with physicians on time and cost issues.
